newsitem.title: UK: Hazlewood says BSE to hit H1 pretax profits.
newsitem.headline: Hazlewood says BSE to hit H1 pretax profits.

text.p: UK food processing and fresh meats group Hazlewood Foods Plc said on Thursday that before the loss of its Charles Turner paper unit, first half pretax profits would be "broadly similar" to last year.

Hazlewood Foods blamed consumer concerns about catching the human equivalent of "mad cow" disease, or BSE, and told shareholders at the annual meeting that trading conditions remained "very challenging".
Hazlewood has said that the sale of Charles Turner would gve rise to a book loss of 4.5 million in 1996/97.

"The consumer concerns about BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy), and the knock-on effect of higher prices for pork and chicken, are having a significantly adverse impact on our meat operations, but have been less significant for convenience foods where we have benefited from product substitution," Peter Barr told shareholders.
Barr said the company was continuing to reposition its business "for growth and improved returns".
He added that with capital expenditure returning to substantially lower levels, cash generation was strongly positive.
